blocks.content: 1. WHAT IS A NOUN?

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Nouns are categorized into countable and uncountable types, with uncountable nouns forming a frequent trap in SSC questions.
Certain nouns appear plural in form but take singular verbs, while others exist exclusively as plural nouns.
Subject-verb agreement for collective nouns depends on whether the group acts as a unified unit or as individual members.
The phrase 'One of' requires a plural noun followed by a singular verb.
Joint possession and separate possession require distinct apostrophe placements.

blocks.content:
A noun is a naming word. It names a person, place, thing, idea, quality, emotion, or state.



Every sentence in English revolves around nouns because the subject and object are usually nouns.



Examples:

• Rohan is studying. (Person)

• Mumbai is crowded. (Place)

• The table is broken. (Thing)

• Honesty is admired. (Quality)



Why Nouns Matter in SSC Exams:

Many grammar mistakes occur because students fail to identify whether a noun is singular, plural, countable, or uncountable. Once you master nouns, a large portion of error-detection questions becomes easy.
2. HOW TO IDENTIFY A NOUN

Ask the following questions:



• Who? → Person

• Where? → Place

• What? → Thing

• What idea or feeling? → Abstract noun



Example:

The child showed great courage.



Child → noun (person)

Courage → noun (quality)
3. TYPES OF NOUNS – WITH CLEAR UNDERSTANDING

Proper Noun:

Names a specific person, place, or organization.

Always begins with a capital letter.



Example:

India, Shakespeare, the Ganga



Common Noun:

General name of a class or category.



Example:

city, boy, river



Collective Noun:

Represents a group acting as one unit.



Example:

team, committee, army



Abstract Noun:

Cannot be seen or touched — only felt.



Example:

freedom, honesty, happiness



Material Noun:

Refers to substances or materials.



Example:

gold, water, cotton
4. COUNTABLE vs UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS (MOST IMPORTANT SSC AREA)

COUNTABLE NOUNS:

These nouns can be counted and have plural forms.



Example:

book → books

apple → apples



They can be used with:

• many

• few

• several

• a number of



UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS:

These cannot be counted individually.



Examples:

advice, furniture, luggage, information, equipment, bread, traffic



IMPORTANT RULE:

Uncountable nouns DO NOT take plural forms.



Incorrect: advices

Correct: advice



Incorrect: informations

Correct: information



Use partitive expressions instead:

• a piece of advice

• an item of furniture

• a slice of bread
5. COMMON SSC TRAP – UNCOUNTABLE NOUN LIST

Memorize these frequently tested nouns:



information

advice

furniture

luggage

equipment

scenery

traffic

work

knowledge

progress



Example Error:

Incorrect: The sceneries were beautiful.

Correct: The scenery was beautiful.
6. NOUNS THAT LOOK PLURAL BUT ARE SINGULAR

Some nouns end in 's' but take singular verbs.



Examples:

news

mathematics

physics

politics

economics



Example:

The news is shocking. (NOT are)
7. NOUNS THAT EXIST ONLY IN PLURAL

These nouns are always plural and require plural verbs.



Examples:

scissors

trousers

spectacles

premises

thanks



Example:

The scissors are on the table.



When referring to one unit:

Use "a pair of".



A pair of scissors is missing.
8. IRREGULAR PLURAL NOUNS

Some nouns form plurals without adding 's' or 'es'.



man → men

woman → women

child → children

foot → feet

tooth → teeth

mouse → mice



These must be memorized — there is no shortcut.
9. FOREIGN PLURALS – FREQUENT SSC QUESTIONS

criterion → criteria

phenomenon → phenomena

analysis → analyses

basis → bases

thesis → theses

radius → radii



Example Error:

Incorrect: The criteria is strict.

Correct: The criteria are strict.
10. SAME SINGULAR AND PLURAL FORMS

Some nouns remain unchanged.



sheep

deer

aircraft

species



Example:

Five deer were spotted in the forest.
11. COLLECTIVE NOUN AGREEMENT – LOGIC RULE

When the group acts as ONE → singular verb.



The committee has approved the proposal.



When members act individually → plural verb.



The committee are arguing among themselves.



SSC tests this logical distinction frequently.
12. POSSESSIVE NOUNS – FULL EXPLANATION

Possession shows ownership.



Singular noun:

Add 's.



Riya's book



Plural ending in 's':

Add only apostrophe.



Students' uniforms



Irregular plural:

Children's park
13. JOINT vs SEPARATE POSSESSION

Joint Possession (one thing shared):

Ravi and Mohan's house.



Separate Possession:

Ravi's and Mohan's houses.
14. NOUN USED AS ADJECTIVE

A noun can modify another noun.



Examples:

shoe shop

car engine

chicken soup



IMPORTANT RULE:

The modifier noun stays singular.



Incorrect: shoes shop

Correct: shoe shop
15. 'ONE OF' RULE (SSC FAVORITE)

Structure:

One of + plural noun + singular verb.



Example:

One of the students is absent.



Reason:

The subject is "one", not "students".
16. 'A NUMBER OF' vs 'THE NUMBER OF'

A number of → plural verb

The number of → singular verb



Example:

A number of students are protesting.

The number of students is increasing.
17. GENDER IN NOUNS

Masculine → king

Feminine → queen

Common → teacher

Neuter → chair



Modern English prefers gender-neutral forms:

police officer instead of policeman.
18. ABSTRACT NOUN FORMATION

From adjectives:

happy → happiness

strong → strength



From verbs:

decide → decision

grow → growth
19. GERUND vs NOUN (CONFUSION AREA)

A gerund is a verb ending in -ing that acts as a noun.



Swimming is good exercise.



After prepositions → ALWAYS use gerund.



Incorrect: interested to learn

Correct: interested in learning

items: Uncountable nouns (such as advice, information, furniture, luggage) never take plural forms or indefinite articles ('a'/'an').
'One of' is always followed by a plural noun and a singular verb.
'A number of' takes a plural noun and a plural verb, whereas 'The number of' takes a plural noun and a singular verb.

blocks.content: 20. HIGH-PROBABILITY SSC RULES

1. Never pluralize uncountable nouns.

2. Memorize irregular plurals.

3. Use singular verb after "one of".

4. Understand collective noun logic.

5. Learn foreign plural forms.

6. Use partitive expressions correctly.
21. COMMON SSC ERRORS

Incorrect: He gave me many advices.

Correct: He gave me much advice.



Incorrect: One of my friend is here.

Correct: One of my friends is here.



Incorrect: The furniture are expensive.

Correct: The furniture is expensive.
22. PRACTICE QUESTIONS (SSC LEVEL)

Fill in the blanks:



1. One of the players ___ injured. (is/are)

2. The furniture ___ expensive. (is/are)

3. A number of students ___ absent. (is/are)



Answers:

is, is, are
23. CHAPTER SUMMARY

Nouns are the backbone of English grammar.



Key Takeaways:



• Identify countable vs uncountable nouns.

• Avoid plural errors.

• Master irregular and foreign plurals.

• Apply possession rules correctly.

• Watch for SSC trap patterns.
